benchmarks.quantity: best-site illumination and longest darkness on the Shackleton-de Gerlache ridge
benchmarks.source: Glaser et al. 2014, Icarus 243, 78-90 (LOLA 20 m/pixel DTM, 19-year study)
benchmarks.sourceLocator: Connecting Ridge results: 92.27% at 2 m, 95.65% at 10 m; longest continuous darkness typically 3-5 days
benchmarks.modelSimplification: Cross-check only: the 117 h default longest shadow sits inside the 3-5 day range, while the 0.71 default fraction is deliberately more conservative than the best site

benchmarks.quantity: polar water-extractor mass and heater power for the NASA baseline case
benchmarks.source: Kleinhenz & Paz 2020, Case Studies for Lunar ISRU Systems Utilizing Polar Water, AIAA 2020-4042
benchmarks.sourceLocator: Table 3 (15 t water in 225 days, 5 wt%, 75% extraction efficiency); Fig. 8 water-extractor mass (~330 kg, read from log scale, incl. 20% growth + 15% structure margins); Sec. IV.B water extractor ~20 kW incl. 20% power margin, i.e. ~16.7 kW
benchmarks.modelSimplification: Calibration anchor, not independent validation: the kIceExtractorMass and etaSubHeater defaults were derived from this case, so agreement confirms the derivation. Linear scaling with regolith throughput is conservative at larger plants (the study's Fig. 9A is sub-linear).

benchmarks.quantity: electrolysis power, LOX/LH2 liquefaction power, and liquefier and electrolyzer mass for the NASA baseline propellant case
benchmarks.source: Kleinhenz & Paz 2020, Case Studies for Lunar ISRU Systems Utilizing Polar Water, AIAA 2020-4042
benchmarks.sourceLocator: Table 3 (15 t water to 13 t O2 + 1.7 t H2 over 225 days less 48 h commissioning, i.e. 67.26 kg/day water); Fig. 8 subsystem mass and ridge power, measured on the log axes and checked against the stated totals (ridge 2.6 t and 46 kW, mine 0.49 t and 22 kW, tankers 1.8 t). Electrolyzer 21.0 kW, H2 liquefaction 20.3 kW, and O2 liquefaction 3.94 kW include a 20% power margin, removed here; masses (electrolyzer 47 + dryers 51 kg, H2 liquefaction 1,753 kg, O2 liquefaction 150 kg) include the study's growth and structure margins.
benchmarks.modelSimplification: Calibration anchor, not independent validation: secCondLh2, secCondLox, kLiquefierLh2, kLiquefierLox, and kElectrolyzerMass were derived from this case, so their agreement confirms the derivation. Electrolysis power is the independent check (cell voltage 1.8 V at 95% Faradaic efficiency) and runs about 10% low; the study's figure includes pumps and balance of plant. Linear scaling with product rate is conservative for larger plants, most of all for H2 liquefaction.

benchmarks.quantity: polar mine excavator mass and power for the NASA baseline case
benchmarks.source: Kleinhenz & Paz 2020, Case Studies for Lunar ISRU Systems Utilizing Polar Water, AIAA 2020-4042
benchmarks.sourceLocator: Table 3 (398 t of icy regolith over 225 days less 48 h commissioning; 20 cm of overburden over a 30 cm mined depth); Sec. IV.C (two RASSOR excavators); Fig. 8 excavator mass (~161 kg) and mine power (~212 W), measured on the log axes, both including the study's margins.
benchmarks.modelSimplification: Comparison, not calibration: the model sizes a continuous fleet at 0.0244 kg per kg/day of soil moved with no margin (Guerrero-Gonzalez & Zabel 2023), about 73 kg here. The study rounds up to two whole 66 kg RASSORs and adds its 20% growth margin (2 x 66 x 1.2 = 158 kg). Its excavators also idle while the extractor hopper is full, so they draw less power than the model's 10.1 kJ per kg of soil moved.

benchmarks.quantity: reduction reactor mass added by feeding sized soil instead of an ilmenite concentrate
benchmarks.source: Eagle Engineering 1988, Conceptual Design of a Lunar Oxygen Pilot Plant, EEI 88-182
benchmarks.sourceLocator: Sec. 6.3.5 and Fig. 6-21: 144 t/yr LOX at 90% duty (438.4 kg/day running), nuclear; process mass 12.5 t with magnetic separation and 18.1 t without, measured on the figure's axis (totals 47.2 and 51.1 t as stated)
benchmarks.modelSimplification: Calibration anchor, not independent validation: kIlmBedMass was derived from this trade, so agreement confirms the derivation. The whole increase is charged to the fluidized bed, as Eagle's text attributes it (a wider, more massive reactor for the larger feed); the linear scaling carries no economy of scale between Eagle's 144 and 1,000 t/yr plants.

benchmarks.quantity: apparent activation energy of ilmenite reduction by hydrogen
benchmarks.source: Zhao & Shadman 1991, Kinetics and mechanism of ilmenite reduction with hydrogen, Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 30(9); Eagle Engineering 1988, EEI 88-182, Sec. 4; Briggs & Sacco 1991, Hydrogen reduction mechanisms of ilmenite between 823 and 1353 K, J. Mater. Res. 6(3)
benchmarks.sourceLocator: Zhao & Shadman abstract: 22.3 kcal/mol apparent over 807-1014 C (synthetic ilmenite, under 45 um). Eagle Sec. 4 cites complete reduction in 2 h at 873 K and 0.25 h at 1,073 K, i.e. R ln 8 / (1/873 - 1/1073) = 80.9 kJ/mol, and equilibrium per-pass H2 conversion of 10.5% at 1,000 C and 7% at 900 C, i.e. R ln 1.5 / (1/1173 - 1/1273) = 50.4 kJ/mol for a bed held near equilibrium. Briggs & Sacco abstract: 43.2 kcal/mol under reaction control at 823-1023 K.
benchmarks.modelSimplification: The default is Zhao & Shadman's value and the input spans the others. Lab rates on fine powder are 10 to 100 times faster than Eagle's design point (90% in 4 h at 1,000 C), whose bed approaches the reaction's gas equilibrium; so only the temperature dependence is taken from the lab, and the rate itself is pinned to Eagle's design. A gas-limited bed may follow the weaker, equilibrium-driven dependence.

benchmarks.quantity: basalt fed, layer mined, and beneficiation power and mass for Eagle's basalt-fed plants
benchmarks.source: Eagle Engineering 1988, Conceptual Design of a Lunar Oxygen Pilot Plant, EEI 88-182
benchmarks.sourceLocator: Table 6-1 (25 vol% ilmenite: 88.23 t basalt fed and 185.74 t mined per t LOX); Table 6-5 (1,000 t/yr basalt plant, nuclear, 90% duty: beneficiation 526 kW and 73.4 t)
benchmarks.modelSimplification: Calibration anchor: the chain's fractions are Eagle's Table 6-1 values, and eIlmComminution and kIlmComminutionMass were derived from Table 6-5, so agreement confirms the derivation, not the physics.

benchmarks.quantity: basalt-fed plant relative to the soil-fed plant at 1,000 t/yr
benchmarks.source: Eagle Engineering 1988, Conceptual Design of a Lunar Oxygen Pilot Plant, EEI 88-182
benchmarks.sourceLocator: Table 6-5: basalt 2,380 kW and 201.7 t against soil 2,988 kW and 243.8 t, both nuclear at 90% duty
benchmarks.modelSimplification: Comparison, not calibration: only beneficiation was fitted to the basalt plant. The model's power ratio comes out near Eagle's; its mass ratio is closer to one because Eagle's basalt process area is 13 t lighter than its soil one for the same concentrate, a difference the model, whose reactor follows the concentrate, does not reproduce.

benchmarks.quantity: Bond's-law grinding energy for basalt, 100 mm to 0.1 mm
benchmarks.source: Bond's third theory of comminution, with Eagle Engineering 1988's basalt work index (App. A.5, Eqn. 37: 20.41 kWh/t)
benchmarks.modelSimplification: Cross-check only: grinding alone is well under the calibrated 169 kJ/kg, which also carries the fine screens, magnetic separation, and handling.
